messages:
Eva: quick heads-up from the APAC perf canary after yesterday's kernel rollout — noticed a large drop in prefix cache hit-rate and a latency spike for short sequences
Jamal: how big a drop? any idea which part of the stack?
Eva: numbers: apac hit_rate_prefix ~0.46 (was ~0.77 before), median batch_size down from 6->3, p99 gen latency doubled for seq<64. eu/us stayed steady.
Sophia: did the kernel change or batching logic land last night?
Li: the fused-attn tiled kernel (attn_tiled_v2) went out in the same deploy. It has a fast path for aligned vectors and a slower fallback when alignment fails
Eva: profiler shows more small batches hitting the fallback slow_path on APAC nodes. Also noticed cache key churn — many keys include ephemeral fields (trace_id/temp_prompt) coming from older SDKs
Maria: so two orthogonal effects: (1) increased cache-key entropy -> misses, (2) batching/kernel flip -> slower path and poorer KV reuse
Jamal: do we have traces to prove correlation?
Eva: yes, sample snippet from canary logs:
```
2026-02-14T18:03:12Z apac-node-07: prefix_hit=0.46 batch_median=3 kernel=attn_tiled_v2 slow_path=true setup_ms=14 gen_p99_ms=410
2026-02-14T18:03:12Z eu-node-02: prefix_hit=0.79 batch_median=6 kernel=attn_tiled_v2 fast_path=true setup_ms=5 gen_p99_ms=190
```
Li: interesting that eu has larger batches but hits fast path more often. could be client sdk differences or request shape distribution
Sophia: maybe eu clients send more multi-turn flows so prefixes repeat, apac clients more single-turn ephemeral prompts
Maria: action plan suggestions:
- immediate: router-level normalization to drop known-ephemeral keys (safe-list whitelist). ship as traffic rule today
- short-term: canary routing fallback from APAC -> EU for first-N-seconds after route warmup to allow cache prefill
- mid-term: batching heuristic change to bias stable kernel selection for small sequences (kernel pin per-route hint)
- long-term: prefix replication metrics + prefetch classifier for cross-region hot prefixes
Jamal: +1 on hotfix. be careful: normalization must not remove customer identifiers used for auth or billing
Eva: agreed. proposed router safe-list: keep {client_id, org_id, model, route_tag}; drop anything matching /^temp_/ or /^trace_/ and any field named ephemeral_*
Li: runtime change: add route config kernel_hint and hint_ttl_seconds. runtime will prefer pinned kernel when batch shapes allow; fall back after TTL
Maria: what monitoring do we need to validate?
Eva: explicit metrics at 1m granularity: regional_prefix_hit_rate, kernel_slow_path_rate, batch_size_median_p90, gen_p95_p99, replication_lag_seconds, warmed_prefix_count
Jamal: set alerts: if regional_prefix_hit_rate delta > 15% for >5m -> page eng-runtime on-call
Sophia: propose a small canary experiment: route 5% of APAC traffic via eu for 30m and compare hit rates & tails
Eva: infra-bot, can you schedule APAC->EU canary and bump trace sample rate for APAC nodes?
infra-bot: scheduled canary 2026-02-15T03:00:00Z - 2026-02-15T03:30:00Z. trace sampling for APAC set to 25% during window. Eva has start/stop permissions.
Li: I'll pair with Eva on the router PR for normalization and kernel pin config.
Maria: I'll draft the batching heuristic doc and list metrics/dashboards to add.
Jamal: timeline?
Eva: hotfix normalization -> next 3 hours. canary -> tomorrow 03:00 UTC. batching design doc -> EOD Friday. kernel-pin POC -> next week.
Maria: final note for PRs: include one-line root-cause hypothesis (key-entropy + kernel fallback due to batching) and the verification checklist (metrics to monitor). Keep updates short during the deploy window.
Eva: will do, closing thread. I'll post short status in #eng-runtime-canaries when hotfix is live.
